text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: [Pager] GPU pool 'us-west-2-a/gpu-large' capacity_exhaustion detected. Queue growth > 3k reqs, autoscaler failed to allocate new instances. Escalation to on-call.

maya: I'm on it. seeing sustained enqueue and a bunch of 429s from router. Metrics: GPU utilization reported ~82% but available GPU slices look fragmented.

jared: any immediate customer impact?

maya: yes — several high-priority tenants (acct: big-ml-startup + corp-analytics) reporting latency spikes and inference timeouts. Errors: 429 throttles and 500s from runtime when job can't be scheduled.

tia: posting partial logs from scheduler:
```
E0620 19:02:14 scheduler.go:512] allocation failed: no compatible MIG shape for request. free_vram: 4GB, requested: 7GB -> fragmentation
W0620 19:02:18 autoscaler.go:238] scale-up failed: API limit hit or instance launch timeout
```

olivia: autoscaler attempted 6 launches in last 10m, cloud returned throttling on instance create (quota?) but the main problem is binpacking: a lot of 1xA100-MIG slices and leftover 40% of GPUs unusable for the requested 7GB shapes.

khan: can we fallback workloads to smaller model variants or CPU-only for non-critical users?

maya: We have fallback flag for some routes. Kicking progressive fallback for 'embedding-batch' to cpu-fallback v1 for low-tier tenants. Applying now.

samir: FYI, I've seen this pattern before — MIG sizing mismatch between training jobs and inference pools. Training team recently changed slice profile to 1g. Need to check if nodes were reimaged.

jared: Live mitigation idea: 1) drain pods from highly fragmented nodes and force binpack onto larger instances 2) temporarily tighten scheduling to prefer unfragmented nodes 3) if autoscaler still can't provision, trigger emergency hot-standby pool (reserved) and failover routing. Thoughts?

maya: Doing 1 & 2 now. Command I'm running:
```
kubectl get nodes -l gpu_fragmented=true -o name | xargs -n1 kubectl cordon
kubectl drain NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

tia: Be careful — draining will evict running inferences. Coordinate with routing to favor fallback so customer impact is minimized.

olivia: Starting routing change to slowly shift new requests to fallback and lower-tier models. Will keep 20% traffic on primary to let critical SLAs through while we stabilize. :white_check_mark:

khan: autoscaler logs show quota error 403: "Insufficient quota for V100 instances" around 19:05:12. Who owns cloud quotas? ops-cloud?

maya: Paging ops-cloud (cc @jared). Jared can you raise a quota request and temporarily bump the reserved pool?

jared: Opening a support ticket with cloud and also creating a manual allocation from our reserved capacity. If reserved pool used, we should avoid further autoscale churn.

samir: Observing a lot of small pods pinned to single GPU slices; we could consolidate by setting nodeSelector to prefer 'mig=large' for latency-sensitive jobs. I'll propose a policy change.

incident-bot: Incident severity updated to P1. Start time 1972005555. Incident channel: #incidents. Pager: maya -> jared.

maya: quick status: drained 4 fragmented nodes, manually migrated 12 high-latency pods onto 3 large-slice nodes, queue length decreased from 3.1k -> 800 in 12m. Error rate dropping but still elevated for some tenants.

tia: Customer comms drafted (internal):
- Impact: increased latency and 429 throttles for inference requests in us-west-2
- Mitigation: progressive fallback to CPU and smaller model variants, manual re-binning of fragments, reserved pool allocation
- ETA to full recovery: TBD; next update in 20m

olivia: Cloud quota increased temporarily by support (confirmed). Autoscaler retries succeed now, but we're seeing slow churn. New instances are coming up but many land with 1g MIG profile due to image bake profile. Need to ensure instance templates use the correct MIG partitioning.

khan: Can we patch the instance template inline? Or do we need a full reprovision?

samir: We can override at launch with startup-script to re-partition MIG but it's risky; better to update template and launch small handful for validation. I'll spin one validated node manually.

jared: I've put 8 reserved GPUs into the inference pool; should help absorb remaining queue. Also kicked a canary scaleup group with corrected MIG profile.

maya: Queue is now 120 and trending down. Error rate back to baseline for high-tier customers. Low-tier still on fallback for ~45m window. Marking incident as mitigation in-progress.

incident-bot: @maya (on-call) assigned. Next update due 20m.

olivia: ACTIONS to follow-up in postmortem:
- Audit node image pipeline for MIG partitioning defaults (owner: eng-infra)
- Add autoscaler telemetry for quota vs instance launch failures (owner: eng-sre)
- Implement cluster-level packing policy that prefers fewer larger slices for latency-sensitive services (owner: eng-ml)
- Add runbook steps for emergency reserved pool allocation (owner: product-ops)

maya: Handoff note for next oncall: we've stabilized. Manual reserved pool used, autoscaler healthy now. Keep an eye on queue <200 and instance launches error rate. Will link logs and commands in the incident doc.

jared: Thanks everyone — good triage. We'll open a postmortem once we've collected logs and impact metrics. :pray:
